_doc: Tùng Đào Cung, part 1: the Hóa Thần, the Nguyên Anh, the Kết Đan and the dead. World-depth pass, sect writer. Part 2 (tung_dao.2.cast.json): Trúc Cơ. Part 3 (tung_dao.3.cast.json): Luyện Khí.

people.gloss: Light as a wild goose (Lạc Thần Phú: phiên nhược kinh hồng)
people.role: Disciple of the founder; second head of Tùng Đào Cung (690-900), retired to the retreat at Thính Đào Nhãn; the sect's one Hóa Thần
people.appearance: A small, straight old woman with white hair cut at the jaw, a grey-green sash that stirs when there is no wind, and a wolf's tooth on a cord.
people.backstory: Thôi Khinh Hồng was born in 80 on the shore of Hạo Nguyệt Hồ, the daughter of a fisher who swore he had seen a man walk over the water into the moon (A001). At sixteen she followed a hermit into the pine sea because he could tell her which way the wind would turn before it turned. He was Kỳ Tùng Ẩn (ky_tung_an), and she was the first person he taught. When he founded the palace in 200 she was 120 and already its strongest voice (C003), and he had the Wandering Dragon Sash made for her that year. In 455 she killed the white wolf king of Cửu Khúc Xuyên (C093). She held the palace together when he broke the peace with the Pivot and lost (C106), and again when he took the Cold Ford without a writ (C135). When he died in 690 she became the second head (C138), and for two hundred years she made no war. In 900 she handed the regalia to Đàm Tùng Lại (dam_tung_lai) and went down to the retreat at Thính Đào Nhãn (C021). The coast says she saw the Cold Ford War coming and stepped aside. She came out once more, in 1090, to kill Mặc Huyết Sinh with Sở Ngọc Hồ (so_ngoc_ho) and Đỗ Tinh Hà (do_tinh_ha) (C024). She spends her days listening to the pines for the canon's fifteenth layer, which her master never spoke.
people.wants: To hear the fifteenth layer of the Pine Wave canon before she dies, and to hand it to someone who can hold it without a war.
people.secret: Kỳ Tùng Ẩn did not die of old age. At Thiết Tỏa Quan in 508 Chung Hoài Cực's strike cracked his core (C105), and the wound ate his life for 180 years. He marched on the Cold Ford in 668 knowing he was dying, to leave the sect a coast, and Chung let it stand because he knew it too (C136). She retired in 900 because she could neither order a war to keep land taken that way nor order the sect to give it up.

people.gloss: Tùng lại is the sound of wind in pines
people.role: Head of Tùng Đào Cung since 900; the head who lost the Cold Ford and goes to war only for his vassals
people.appearance: A tall, stooped man with a ferryman's hands, who tilts his head before he speaks as if to catch a sound behind him.
people.backstory: Đàm Tùng Lại was born in 520 in Cổ Độ Thành, the ferry town whose men had carried the iron chain of Thiết Tỏa Quan to the river link by link fourteen years before (A054). His father was one of them and never spoke of the war. Thôi Khinh Hồng (thoi_khinh_hong) took the boy at ten for his ear: he could name every boat on the river by the sound of its oars. She gave him the pine name Tùng Lại, the wind in the pines. He became head in 900 at 380 (C021), and within a year Thúy Vi marched under the Pivot's writ (C165). In 905 he ordered the sect off the Cold Ford rather than lose the inner gate on its quays; the governor Giáp Tùng Chi (giap_tung_chi) refused to leave and died there (C166). He fought the Long Lake War for Hàm Nguyệt Trang's pearls (C170) and the Ferry War for Lãng Đào's burned boats (C192), and took no land in either: he goes to war for vassals, never for ground. He has taught more of the living elders than anyone. Ngu Lam Sơn (ngu_lam_son) sends him tea every new year. He drinks it alone and does not answer.
people.wants: To leave a sect that shelters what grows under it rather than one that spreads, and to see Vi Thanh Âm, whom he named heir in 1199, come through the Root Hall's searches whole.
people.secret: He answers none of Ngu's letters because he wrote one in 906, a long one, and the Coiled Root Hall's men took it before it left the palace. It has passed from master to master of that hall, and Nhiếp Cô Tân has held it since 1090. In it Đàm wrote that the Cold Ford was never Tùng Đào's to keep.

people.role: Master of the Coiled Root Hall (war, patrols, discipline); Cold Ford-born, the voice of the sect's old reach
people.appearance: A broad, weathered man who still walks like a fisher on a wet quay, with a governor's seal of green stone at his belt where a sword would hang.
people.backstory: Nhiếp Cô Tân was born in 872 on the quays of Hàn Tân Thành, a fisher's son under Tùng Đào's rule, two doors from a family that kept the name of a dead Thúy Vi warden. When that family's boy, Hướng Dạ Đăng (huong_da_dang), swam the river mouth to Thúy Vi in 881, the governor Giáp Tùng Chi (giap_tung_chi) took the next boy on the street into the pines, to show the quay which side it stood on. That was Nhiếp. He has no pine name: Đàm gives none, and Nhiếp would not take one from him. He keeps his own, the lone ford. In 905 Đàm Tùng Lại (dam_tung_lai) ordered the sect off the coast. Giáp stayed on the quay, and Nhiếp, a Trúc Cơ of 33, carried his master's seal out of the town (C166). He has run the Coiled Root Hall since 1090 and formed his Nascent Soul in 1151. His son Nhiếp Thừa Phong (nhiep_thua_phong) died cutting the rope bridges of the Ngư Ca border in 1174 (A202), and the Ferry War ended with the tolls split and no land changed (C193). He has buried a master and a son for a head who gives everything back. He raised his granddaughter Nhiếp Vãn Đào (nhiep_van_dao) to be the head the sect would need, and in 1199 Đàm named Vi Thanh Âm (vi_thanh_am) instead. Nhiếp did not argue the choice. He saw ink on the heir's hand that night, and his hall has searched her rooms ever since. Since last autumn one of his patrols has also wintered at Tùng Phong Thôn, testing the village children for ears before Vạn Hác's outer gate can reach them.
people.wants: The Cold Ford back, by writ or without one, and the named heir's zither opened before the council while Đàm still sits.
people.secret: In 1172 he sent a patrol of six onto the river-mouth ice to map Thúy Vi's crossings for a winter war, without the head's leave. They never came back (N-thuy_vi-11). He let the sect list them as deserters rather than own the order, and one of them was Lộ Thu Hà's son. He also holds the letter Đàm wrote to Ngu Lam Sơn in 906 and never sent.

people.role: Mistress of the River Hall at Đào Thanh Thành: the dikes, the tolls and the river vassals; the swing vote of the palace
people.appearance: A thin woman in a dark blue robe with river mud always drying on the hem, who carries a green glass lamp even at noon.
people.backstory: Dụ Tĩnh Lưu was born in 690 at Tĩnh Thủy Quán, the Abbey of Still Water on the low bank of the Nine-Bend River, to a lay sister who kept its lamps. In 700 the great flood drowned three villages and the abbey with them (A074). She lived four days on the roof. Two years later the survivors walked to Tùng Đào (V046), and the girl carried the abbey's altar lamp, which she had dug out of the mud. The River Hall's master Hề Tùng Ba (he_tung_ba) taught her the river until Thôi Khinh Hồng (thoi_khinh_hong) took her as a disciple in 712. She has run the River Hall at Đào Thanh Thành since 840 and kept the river vassals, Lãng Đào Môn and Thải Chi Cốc, fed and quiet. Since 1176, when the war had doubled the valley's orphans and halved her tolls, the grain she sends Thải Chi has been paid for in work: the valley's oldest orphans dig the River Hall's dikes on its own reach of the river by the day, and their wages are set against the grain. In 1175 she sat across from Lạc Hà's envoys and split the river tolls (C193). Nhiếp Cô Tân (nhiep_co_tan) has never forgiven the split, and Lạc Hà has never forgiven the terms. In council she votes with whichever side will keep a quay above the flood line, and most of the River Hall's elders are her disciples.
people.wants: A dike from Đào Thanh Thành to the river's last bend that no flood can top, and no head who would ever have to choose which bank drowns.
people.secret: Hề Tùng Ba told her on his deathbed in 840 that in 700 he opened the River Hall's sluice array to save Đào Thanh Thành's quays and sent the flood onto the abbey's bank. She has run his hall for 360 years so that no one else will make that choice, and she has never told the abbey's children.

people.role: First elder of Tùng Đào Cung (age 400) and keeper of the Hall of Voices, where the unwritten canon is taught
people.appearance: A plump, quick woman in grey-green with a teaching fan always in her hand, who laughs before she answers and remembers what you told her forty years ago.
people.backstory: Hồ Tùng Nguyệt was born in 800 in Quy Điểu Trấn on the long lake, where the pearl market is held on the ice (A011), to a family of pearl brokers. Đàm Tùng Lại (dam_tung_lai) took her at eleven, his first disciple, and in 890 Thôi Khinh Hồng (thoi_khinh_hong) gave her a pine name. She has run the Hall of Voices for two centuries. Every method in Tùng Đào is taught by voice, and more of the canon lives in her than in anyone but the two heads; there are inner disciples who have never heard it from another mouth. She is warm, she forgets nothing, and she forgives almost everything. She keeps the ten-yearly border talks with Thúy Vi civil across the table from Biện Vãn Tình (bien_van_tinh) and Hướng Dạ Đăng (huong_da_dang). She is 400, at the last stage of Kết Đan and in good health. At the border talks of 1190 Hướng Dạ Đăng quoted the primer's fourth line to her across the table, word for word. Since 1194 she has paid a young man named Phù Liên Kiều (phu_lien_kieu) to sit in Thúy Vi's outer gate, where nothing is locked, and list what its shelves hold of the pines' canon.
people.wants: To know how much of the pines' canon Thúy Vi has written down from the Cold Ford families, and to bring that book home or burn it.
people.secret: She pays the spy from the Coiled Root Hall's purse, telling Nhiếp Cô Tân the boy is learning Thúy Vi's Haze Walk for his winter crossing. She has no intention of giving Nhiếp the Walk. What she asks the boy for, in every letter, is the shelf list.

people.role: The head's true disciple, named heir in 1199; holds the canon to its twelfth layer
people.appearance: A slight young woman with ink on the side of her right hand, which she keeps in her sleeve, and a seven-string zither on her back.
people.backstory: Vi Thanh Âm was born in 1040 above a lamp shop in Tùng Hạ Thị, the market that grew from the pilgrims' tents under the pines (A049). At eight she repeated the whole Listening Pine Primer back to the outer gate's steward after hearing it once, and the steward walked her up to the palace that night. Đàm Tùng Lại (dam_tung_lai) has taught her ever since. She formed her Golden Core in 1160, the youngest in the sect for three hundred years, and she holds the canon to its twelfth layer, every song of the Hall of Voices and a good part of what Vạn Hác Viện plays. At the new-year listening of 1199 Đàm named her heir, and the Coiled Root Hall did not argue. Its master Nhiếp Cô Tân (nhiep_co_tan), who says a head should have seen a war, saw the ink on her hand that night, and his hall has searched her rooms whenever she leaves them since. She has not seen a war. She has seen arts die. In 1136 an old ward-singer of the Array Hall died in seclusion with three ward-songs no one else had heard, and they went with him. Since then she has been doing something no disciple of Tùng Đào has done in a thousand years.
people.wants: To be worthy of the headship, and to keep any more of the canon from dying in one person's head.
people.secret: She is writing the canon down. Four hundred pages of it, in a cipher of zither tablature, are hidden inside the body of her zither. It is the gravest taboo the sect has.

people.role: Master of the Array Hall: the palace wards and the River Hall's sluices; the man who broke the ice in 904
people.appearance: A long-boned old man with frost-white eyebrows and blue-stained fingers, who sits very still and counts under his breath.
people.backstory: Cận Tùng Hàn was born in 760 in Lâu Thuyền Trấn, a boat-builders' town on the river, and learned to lay arrays the way his father laid keels, from the bottom up. Thôi Khinh Hồng (thoi_khinh_hong) took him in 835 and named him Tùng Hàn, the pine in winter, when he made elder in 900. In the Cold Ford War he held the river mouth. In the winter of 904 Thúy Vi's Tân Hàn Chu (tan_han_chu) led forty disciples across the ice at night, and his nine flags were waiting under it. The ice broke (N-thuy_vi-06). It was the sect's only victory of the war, and it changed nothing: the ford went back to Thúy Vi the next year (C166). The palace honours him for that night, and he has never once spoken of it. He keeps the palace wards and the River Hall's sluice arrays, plays go with the steward Từ Tích Cốc (tu_tich_coc), and has refused three times to lay a crossing on the river-mouth ice for Nhiếp Cô Tân (nhiep_co_tan).
people.wants: To keep his flags rolled, and to see Khuông Hàn Ly hold the Array Hall after him without ever laying a road on that ice.
people.secret: He heard them under the ice that night for most of an hour, and he did not open the array to let any of them up. Now Khuông Hàn Ly brings him every flag she makes for Nhiếp's crossing to check, and he retunes each one so that the road will hold a patrol and break under a company.

people.role: Founder of Tùng Đào Cung (year 200, at 130); lies under the oldest pine in the palace yard
people.backstory: Kỳ Tùng Ẩn was born in 70 in the Wild Age and grew up alone in the pine sea of Thâm Tùng Hải, learning to cultivate by listening to it. In 200, at 130, he founded Tùng Đào Cung among the pines with his first disciple, Thôi Khinh Hồng (thoi_khinh_hong) (C003), and chanted his canon to every disciple himself. He was a hermit who could not stop gathering: the river basin in 260 (C066), the long lake in 330 (C077), the fallen abbeys of the north. In 270 he drank three days with Thiên Xu's founder Chung Hoài Cực (chung_hoai_cuc) and kept the peace for two centuries (C070). In 502 he broke it and marched on the heart of the continent with Lạc Hà (C103), and lost at Thiết Tỏa Quan (C105). In 668 he took the Cold Ford without a writ (C135), and his old friend let it stand (C136). He died in 690 at 620, and every pine around the long lake dropped its needles at once (A010, C138). He never spoke the fifteenth layer of his canon to anyone.

people.gloss: Walking on the waves (Lạc Thần Phú: lăng ba vi bộ)
people.role: Lake Warden: keeps the Lake Hall at Noãn Ốc and watches Băng Tâm's boats on the north shore of Hạo Nguyệt Hồ
people.appearance: A short, wind-burned woman in a sealskin cloak with a bronze mirror at her hip.
people.backstory: Born in Hàn Yên Thôn, where the smoke once froze above the chimneys (A003), she was a skiff girl of ninety when the Long Lake War began (C170), and she ran the night signals across Hạo Nguyệt Hồ with a bronze mirror. She has kept the Lake Hall at Noãn Ốc since 1010, counts Băng Tâm's boats on the north shore every dawn, and once a year, when Kiều Nguyệt Châu (kieu_nguyet_chau) of Hàm Nguyệt Trang makes the long journey to the Lake Hall with her pearls, drinks with her while she counts them. She wants an inner gate for the lake's Water-rooted children, and the canon has none.
people.wants: An inner gate at Noãn Ốc for the lake's Water-rooted children, and Băng Tâm's skiffs fishing only the north shore.
people.secret: Every dusk she flashes three signals across the lake with the bronze mirror, and Mẫn Băng Hà (man_bang_ha), skiff captain of the frost coast, answers from the far shore; she is arranging a quiet truce for the ice-fishing season and has told neither the palace nor Kiều Nguyệt Châu.

people.role: Steward of the palace: the granaries at Lâm Hạ Trấn, the resin trade and the treasury
people.appearance: A neat, round-faced man with an abacus of pine-nut beads that he works without looking.
people.backstory: A grain merchant's son from Tùng Gian Thành, he keeps the sect's granaries in the shade at Lâm Hạ Trấn (A073), its resin trade and its treasury, and he is the one man in the palace who knows exactly how poor seven vassals make it. He learned his figures from Dụ Tĩnh Lưu (du_tinh_luu) on the river toll books. Nhiếp Cô Tân (nhiep_co_tan) asks him every year what a winter war would cost. Every year he answers to the last stone, and the answer is too much.
people.wants: To die with the treasury solvent and the Root's winter war never funded.
people.secret: He is skimming one measure in a hundred from the Lâm Hạ granaries into a hidden famine store, so the sect can eat through a winter war it must not fight; Tôn Mạch Sinh (ton_mach_sinh) guards the door and thinks it is mouse-bait.

people.role: Captain of the Coiled Root Hall's patrols and tiger hunter of the deep pines
people.appearance: A lean, scarred man in a tiger-skin half-cape with the claw marks still in it.
people.backstory: His great-grandparents were among the survivors of Hổ Khiếu Trấn who planted a green pine for each of their dead at Thanh Tùng Thôn (A058), and he grew up among those trees. He hunts the tigers of the deep pines, leads the Coiled Root Hall's patrols, and has been Nhiếp Cô Tân's (nhiep_co_tan) right hand for eighty years. In 1172 he chose the six men for the river-mouth patrol and read the order aloud to them by the reed-camp fire without looking at the seal. He has started to look now. Since the naming of 1199 he has led the hall's searches of the heir's rooms, and twice he has lifted her zither off its stand and weighed it in his hands.
people.wants: To put the six men's names on a post at the reed camp, and to learn whose order he really read.
people.secret: Each night he carves six names on pine stakes and buries them under the green pines of Thanh Tùng Thôn, so that Hứa Niệm Tùng (hua_niem_tung) tends graves the roll says do not exist.

people.role: Keeper of the Tide Rite at the empty pavilion of Vọng Triều Các; the last who holds its method whole
people.appearance: A gaunt man with salt in his beard, barefoot in all weathers.
people.backstory: The disciples of Vọng Triều Các came to the palace in 470, two years after their master walked into the winter sea to cultivate the tide (V035), and they kept his method alive inside Tùng Đào for 730 years as the Tide Rite. Bạc Hải Âm is the last of them who holds it whole. He lives at the empty pavilion on the coast and swims in the sea every midwinter. He has told Dụ Tĩnh Lưu (du_tinh_luu) that when Nhâm Thu Lãng (nham_thu_lang) can hold the method alone, he will walk out after the founder.
people.wants: To hold the Tide Rite until Nhâm Thu Lãng can carry it, and then to walk out into the sea.
people.secret: Each midwinter he teaches Phan Ba Sinh (phan_ba_sinh) the Rite's last tide in secret, because Nhâm Thu Lãng is too slow, and means to leave the method to the faster boy.

people.role: Keeper of the Incense Hall in the gardens of Lãnh Hương Viện; makes the sticks that time the listening
people.appearance: A tall woman whose sleeves smell of agarwood and cold plum, with soot under her nails.
people.backstory: Her family were the incense makers of Lãnh Hương Viện, taken in by the sect in 890 when the academy's last master died in seclusion without an heir (V004). She grows the herbs that still come up untended in its old courtyards and makes the one stick that burns at dawn and the one at dusk in the palace censer. Đàm Tùng Lại (dam_tung_lai) taught her the canon; her grandmother taught her the incense, by voice, as the sect teaches everything.
people.wants: To make one stick that burns an extra breath, and to learn why the new resin burns short.
people.secret: She has traced the thin resin to Hầu Thiện Kế's (hau_thien_ke) side trade and is quietly buying back the good lots with her own stipend.

people.backstory: Born in Đào Thanh Thành, she has the river town's gift for a long, pleasant meeting that ends with the other side paying. She carried the sect's complaint against Lạc Hà to Thiên Xu after the Ferry War (C193), and Doãn Ngọc Hành (doan_ngoc_hanh) set it aside with a smile; she has not forgiven the smile. She took in the earthquake orphan Trịnh Ức Vân (trinh_uc_van) in 1134 (V052) and has made her a better envoy than herself.
people.wants: To make Doãn Ngọc Hành's smile cost the Pivot something, and to leave an envoy better than herself.
people.secret: She keeps one meeting in ten for herself, a private tithe of tea-money from the vassals' gifts, which she calls the envoy's costs; Trịnh Ức Vân (trinh_uc_van) keeps the true accounts and has not yet asked.

He laid the sluice arrays that keep the Nine-Bend River off the city's quays, chanted the first version of the Rain on the Pine Sea canon in 760, and in 700, the year of the great flood, moved Đào Thanh Thành's quays up the bank (A074). He taught the river to a drowned abbey's orphan, Dụ Tĩnh Lưu (du_tinh_luu), and died with her holding his hand.
